pr.title: Add bounded retries to webhook delivery
pr.head: feature/webhook-retry-budget
pr.tldr: Webhook delivery now retries transient failures with bounded backoff. Permanent failures stop immediately, which protects downstream services from repeated invalid requests.

why.problem: The delivery worker treats every send failure the same. A short network interruption loses a webhook, while repeated retries of a rejected payload waste worker capacity.
what: Classify transient and permanent send failures.
Retry transient failures with three attempts and exponential backoff.
Record a terminal failure after the retry budget is exhausted.
Add tests for recovery, permanent failure, and exhausted retries.

architecture.caption: The worker checks the retry policy before each send. Exhausted jobs move to the dead-letter queue.
architecture.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Worker[Delivery worker] --> Policy[Retry policy]
  Policy --> Sender[Webhook sender]
  Sender --> Endpoint[Remote endpoint]
  Policy -- exhausted --> DeadLetter[(Dead-letter queue)]

changes.title: Retry-aware delivery worker
changes.why: The worker applies the retry policy around each webhook send and returns a terminal result when the budget ends.

blocks.label: Delivery loop

changes.title: Bounded retry policy
changes.why: The policy retries only transient errors and caps attempts with a short exponential delay.

blocks.label: Policy

changes.title: Failure classification
changes.why: The sender turns response status into a retryable or permanent error before the worker decides what to do next.

blocks.label: Send result

data.caption: Each delivery record stores retry state so a resumed worker can continue from the last attempt.

fields.note: classified error from the latest send

reasons: A policy mistake could delay delivery or drop a transient failure.
The attempt cap bounds extra traffic to the remote endpoint.
Existing successful deliveries keep the same single-send path.

tradeoffs: Exponential backoff improves recovery but increases delivery time during an outage.
Permanent failures stop early but require accurate response classification.
focus: Check that status classification matches the endpoint contract.
Confirm the attempt count is persisted before a worker restart.
Verify exhausted jobs receive a clear terminal status.
